# ocean3d

**ocean3d** is an R package for three-dimensional marine spatial
analysis of species ranges, fisheries, and depth-stratified
oceanographic data. It grew out of work on sharks, rays, and chimaeras,
with the functions generalising to any marine taxon or spatial layer.

The three-dimensional marine environment poses a unique challenge for
spatial analyses. Most conventional GIS workflows represent space as a
two-dimensional plane. This abstraction fails to capture the range of
depths and vertical overlap of marine habitat. Fisheries also operate at
different depths depending on gear type and target species, creating
depth-specific patterns of threat exposure that require analysis in 3D
volume rather than 2D planes to quantify. `ocean3d` provides documented
workflows and reusable functions for:

- extracting values from depth-stratified oceanographic rasters within
  user-defined geographic areas and depth windows;
- characterising the abiotic habitat (e.g., temperature, dissolved
  oxygen) of marine species using IUCN Red List ranges and World Ocean
  Atlas 2023 climatologies;
- calculating three-dimensional overlap between species distributions,
  fisheries effort, and other spatial layers;
- producing depth-aware maps and depth-profile plots of species ranges,
  environmental conditions, and cumulative fishing pressure.

## How it works

Species ranges and other spatial layers are usually stored as 2D maps,
but marine species and activities also occupy a depth range, bounded by
the seafloor. `ocean3d` combines a 2D range, a depth range, bathymetry
and gridded environmental data into one 3D representation, so you can
ask, for example, which temperatures occur within a species’ 3D
distribution.

![A species’ range as a 2D polygon on a bathymetry map (A) and as a 3D
distribution between the surface and the seafloor in a vertical
cross-section (B). Panel C shows the inputs ocean3d combines: the range
polygon, the depth range, bathymetry and temperature at several depths,
to find the temperatures within the 3D
distribution.](articles/figures/Figure1_conceptual3Ddistribution.png)

A species’ range as a 2D polygon on a bathymetry map (A) and as a 3D
distribution between the surface and the seafloor in a vertical
cross-section (B). Panel C shows the inputs ocean3d combines: the range
polygon, the depth range, bathymetry and temperature at several depths,
to find the temperatures within the 3D distribution.

In order to represent the 3D space in the ocean, we use a stacked-raster
approach built on `terra`. We call this the Spatial Voxel Model, with
the class `SpatVoxel`. Using this `SpatVoxel`, we can represent any
number of spatial phenomena in the ocean, including species
distributions, fishing effort, and oceanographic variables.

`ocean3d` has three representations for 3D geometry:

- A `SpatVector3D` holds points, lines and polygons with depth and time,
  such as tag detections, dive tracks or a protected area from 0 to
  200 m. Each polygon has a top and a bottom depth. Build one with
  [`as_vector3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_vector3d.md).
- A `SpatEnvelope` stores one continuous `[depth_min, depth_max]`
  interval per grid cell, bounded by the seafloor. It suits ranges with
  defined limits in area and depth, such as IUCN species ranges and
  fishery footprints.
- A `SpatVoxel` stores a value at each of a set of depth levels in every
  cell. It suits continuous values, such as temperature or the modelled
  probability of occurrence, and can hold interior gaps and overhangs,
  because it has a value at every depth rather than one depth range.

![The same example as a SpatVector3D, a polygon with a top and bottom
surface (A); a SpatEnvelope, its depth_min and depth_max on a grid above
the seafloor (B); and a SpatVoxel, presence at depth levels from 50 to
500 m (C). The curved top and bottom surfaces and vector3d_to_envelope()
are planned: a SpatVector3D polygon currently has one depth
range.](articles/figures/Comparison_SpatVector3D_SpatEnvelope_SpatVoxel.png)

The same example as a SpatVector3D, a polygon with a top and bottom
surface (A); a SpatEnvelope, its depth_min and depth_max on a grid above
the seafloor (B); and a SpatVoxel, presence at depth levels from 50 to
500 m (C). The curved top and bottom surfaces and vector3d_to_envelope()
are planned: a SpatVector3D polygon currently has one depth range.

*[`vector3d_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vector3d_to_envelope.md)
and the curved top and bottom surfaces in panel A are planned. Today
each `SpatVector3D` polygon has one depth range.*

Functions convert between these representations.
[`vect_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vect_to_envelope.md)
turns a species range polygon and its observed depth range into a
`SpatEnvelope` bounded by the seafloor, and
[`envelope_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/envelope_to_voxel.md)
places it on the depth levels of a `SpatVoxel`, as in panels B and C
above.

This package includes utilities for working with commonly used datasets
in marine habitat spatial analyses, including IUCN Red List, World Ocean
Atlas, GEBCO, Copernicus Marine, and Global Fishing Watch.

## Existing spatial analysis packages and their limitations

Several R packages and other tools handle depth or 3D data, and
`ocean3d` builds on terra, sf, ncdf4 and CFtime. None of the tools below
answers 3D spatial queries on gridded marine data on its own: which
cells and depths a species, fishery or other layer occupies above the
seafloor, where two of them overlap in 3D, and what environmental values
fall inside.

| Tool | What it does | Limitations for 3D spatial analysis |
|----|----|----|
| [terra](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/) | Raster and vector analysis. A multi-layer `SpatRaster` can record one depth per layer with [`terra::depth()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/depth.html). | Functions such as `mask()`, `extract()` and `zonal()` treat layers as a stack and don’t use their depths. A raster can’t store a depth range per cell, and there is no 3D intersect, overlap or volume. In [our trial](https://github.com/Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d/issues/112), terra read 19 of 29 netCDF test cases correctly, and its errors were silent. |
| [sf](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) | Vector geometry and spatial queries (buffers, clips, intersections). | Geometries can carry Z coordinates, but operations such as `st_intersection()`, `st_buffer()` and `st_area()` work in 2D and ignore them. No raster data. |
| [stars](https://r-spatial.github.io/stars/) | Arrays with any number of dimensions (data cubes), including depth and time. | No class for a depth range per cell, and no 3D intersect or volume. In [our trial](https://github.com/Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d/issues/112), extracting 2 points from a large file through a stars proxy took 198–243 s or tried to allocate 51–56 GB, and slicing a proxy dropped the decoded time. |
| [rgl](https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl/), [rayshader](https://www.rayshader.com/) | 3D visualisation. | They draw 3D scenes. They don’t do spatial queries or calculate volumes. |
| [lidR](https://r-lidar.github.io/lidRbook/), [rTLS](https://github.com/Antguz/rTLS) | 3D point clouds from LiDAR and terrestrial laser scanning. | Built for dense point clouds of land surfaces and vegetation. They don’t work on gridded ocean data with depth levels, a seafloor and time. |
| [PostGIS](https://postgis.net/docs/PostGIS_Special_Functions_Index.html#PostGIS_3D_Functions) | 3D functions on vector geometry in a PostgreSQL database. | Its 3D functions are for vector geometry, and its rasters have bands but no depth. Using it means running a database outside R. |

## Installation

You can install the development version of ocean3d from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d")
```

## Learning resources

New to ocean3d? Watch the recording of the EEA 2026 workshop, which
walks through the package and its main workflows:

[![EEA 2026 workshop
recording](https://img.youtube.com/vi/KOjN21PWtHk/hqdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KOjN21PWtHk)

## Function overview

An analysis in `ocean3d` has three steps: **build** 3D objects from your
inputs, **intersect** them with each other or with the data, and
**summarise** the result as volumes, overlaps or statistics. The
functions below are grouped by step (see the [package design in
SPEC.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/SPEC.html#package-design-build-intersect-summarise)).

### Which input each function takes

`ocean3d` currently has two data models for gridded data, and each
function takes one of them:

| Input | Functions | Reads with |
|----|----|----|
| netCDF files (paths, open `ncdf4` connections or a file table) | [`extract_to_point()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_point.md) and its [`extract2d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract2d.md) / `extract3d_*()` wrappers, [`extract_to_buffer()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_buffer.md), [`extract_to_track()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_track.md) | ncdf4, only the cells each observation needs; keeps the time dimension |
| `SpatVoxel` / `SpatEnvelope` (3D classes built on [`terra::SpatRaster`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/SpatRaster-class.html)) | the build, intersect and volume functions and `mask()` | terra; one time step per voxel |

A voxel can’t be passed to
[`extract_to_point()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_point.md).
[`extract_to_area()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_area.md)
and
[`volume()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/volume.md)
take a voxel or a netCDF file described with
[`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md).
Merging the two into one model with time is planned in
[\#99](https://github.com/Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d/issues/99).
Its first, experimental part is
[`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md),
which describes a netCDF file (such as a World Ocean Atlas file from
[`woa_download()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_download.md)),
a series of files or a voxel in memory as a `SpatProxy` without reading
its values. To use a netCDF file with the voxel functions, describe it
with
[`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md),
crop it to your area with
[`terra::crop()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/crop.html),
and read one time step with
[`as_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_voxel.md);
only the cropped cells are read.

### Build: 3D objects

Input: `SpatRaster` layers, tables of points or lines, and polygons
(`sf`, `SpatVector`). Output: `SpatVoxel`, `SpatEnvelope` or
`SpatVector3D`.

- [`create_study_raster()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/create_study_raster.md)
  — build an empty study-area `SpatRaster` covering the combined extent
  of one or more spatial inputs.
- [`as_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_voxel.md)
  — wrap a multi-depth `SpatRaster` (or a list of single-depth ones) as
  a validated `SpatVoxel`, ordered shallow to deep, with each layer’s
  depth in
  [`terra::depth()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/depth.html).
  This is how gridded data, including netCDF files described with
  [`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md)
  or loaded with terra, enter the voxel model.
- [`as_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_envelope.md)
  — define a 3D envelope with two rasters, with `depth_min` and
  `depth_max` corresponding to the minimum and maximum depths present in
  given cell.
- [`as_vector3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_vector3d.md)
  — build a `SpatVector3D` of points, lines or polygons with depth and
  time, from a table with one row per vertex or from `sf` or
  `SpatVector` geometry.
- [`vect_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vect_to_envelope.md)
  — rasterize a single species range or fishery footprint onto the study
  grid and attach per-cell `depth_min` / `depth_max`, returning a
  `SpatEnvelope`.
- [`envelope_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/envelope_to_voxel.md)
  — expand an envelope onto a set of depth levels.
  [`profile_flat()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_profiles.md)
  and
  [`profile_equal()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_profiles.md)
  set how a cell’s value is spread down the levels it occupies.
- [`voxel_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_to_envelope.md)
  — collapse a voxel to the envelope bounding it, using a predicate on
  the cell values. Lossy: interior gaps are filled.
- [`occupied()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/occupied.md)
  — turn a voxel of values (e.g. temperature) into a presence voxel,
  using a predicate on the cell values.
- [`depths()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/depths.md)
  — read the depth of each layer of a voxel.

### Intersect: 3D spatial query

Input: `SpatVoxel` or `SpatEnvelope`, compared with another 3D object,
`SpatVector3D` polygons, or a 2D object: a `SpatRaster` footprint or
polygons (`SpatVector`, `sf`). A 2D object restricts the domain
horizontally without restricting the depths. `SpatVector3D` polygons
compared with an envelope are first put on its grid, as
[`vector3d_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vector3d_to_envelope.md)
does. With a voxel, they are put on its depth levels one level at a
time, as
[`vector3d_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vector3d_to_voxel.md)
does, so a depth gap between two polygons over one cell stays empty.

Two sets of `SpatVector3D` polygons can also be compared:
[`intersect_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/intersect_3d.md)
returns the polygons they share in outline, depth and time, and
[`intersects_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/intersects_3d.md)
lists, for each polygon of the first set, the polygons of the second it
shares space with.

- `intersect_3d(x, y)` — the shared 3D space between the two inputs.
  Returns an envelope with the shared depth interval, a presence voxel,
  or (for two polygon sets) `SpatVector3D` polygons, depending on
  inputs.
- `intersects_3d(x, y)` — whether inputs share any 3D space. For
  rasters, cell by cell: `TRUE`, `FALSE` (both present but disjoint, or
  only one present), or `NA` (neither present). For two polygon sets, a
  list of the polygons of `y` each polygon of `x` meets.
- `mask(x, mask)` —
  [`terra::mask()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/mask.html)
  made depth-aware. Keeps the values of `x` where the mask domain
  reaches that cell *at that depth*.

### Summarise: 3D volume

Input: `SpatEnvelope`, `SpatVoxel` or `SpatVector3D` polygons. A voxel’s
volume sums the slab each occupied depth level stands for, so interior
gaps cost volume instead of being filled in. A polygon’s volume is its
area times its depth range, measured from the outline rather than a
grid.

- [`volume()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/volume.md)
  — 3D volume (km³) of a domain, as a total or per cell
  (`per_cell = TRUE`, envelopes and voxels only). Measure an overlap
  with `volume(intersect_3d(a, b))`.

### Summarise: environmental extraction from a `SpatVoxel`

Input: a `SpatVoxel` already loaded with terra.

- [`extract_to_area()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_area.md)
  — keep the values of a `SpatVoxel`, or of a netCDF file described with
  [`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md),
  inside an area polygon and a depth band.
- `mask()` (above) — keep a `SpatVoxel`‘s values inside a 3D volume,
  such as a species’ range from
  [`vect_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vect_to_envelope.md).

See
[`vignette("ocean3d")`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/articles/ocean3d.md)
for the full workflow, from a range polygon through to a vertical
profile of the values inside it.

### Summarise: environmental extraction from netCDF files

Input: observations (data frame, tibble, `sf` POINT, matrix, or named
list) and one or more netCDF files. These functions read the files
directly, only the cells each observation needs, and match time as well
as depth. They don’t take a `SpatVoxel`.

- [`extract_to_point()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_point.md)
  — the general engine: match observation points against one or more
  netCDF files. By default a point takes the value of the grid cell that
  contains it (`NA` outside the grid); `spatial_match = "nearest"`
  accepts the nearest cell centre within `max_distance_km`. Time is
  matched to the nearest timestamp and depth by physical depth in
  metres. Returns the input with the extracted values appended,
  structure preserved.
- [`extract2d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract2d.md)
  — for variables with no depth dimension.
- [`extract3d_nearest()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_nearest.md)
  — the valid, non-missing depth layer closest to each observation’s
  depth, so a cell below the seabed does not silently return `NA`.
- [`extract3d_surface()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_surface.md)
  /
  [`extract3d_bottom()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_bottom.md)
  — the physically shallowest depth layer, or the deepest non-missing
  one at that cell.
- [`extract3d_all()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_all.md)
  — nearest, surface and bottom in one pass, as three columns.
- [`extract_to_buffer()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_buffer.md)
  — summarise values within a geodesic circle × depth window × time
  window around each observation, weighted by cell coverage, layer
  thickness and time, or pick the value closest to a target.
- [`extract_to_track()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_track.md)
  — sample points along ordered tracks (e.g. tagging data), extract
  values at them, and optionally summarise per track.

### Data utilities

These download or load public datasets. The loaders return a plain
`SpatRaster`; wrap it with
[`as_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_voxel.md)
or
[`as_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_envelope.md)
to use it with the build, intersect and volume functions above. The
netCDF extraction functions take the downloaded files themselves
(e.g. from
[`woa_download()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_download.md)).

#### IUCN Red List API utilities

Add an IUCN Red List API key to access species-assessment functions.
Sign up and acquire your API key at <https://api.iucnredlist.org/>:

``` r

usethis::edit_r_environ()
# Add the following line to the .Renviron file
# IUCN_REDLIST_KEY="your_iucn_api_key_here"
```

- [`fetch_species_assessments()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/fetch_species_assessments.md)
  — query the IUCN Red List API for taxonomy, Red List category, and
  depth limits, by SIS ID, scientific name, or comprehensive group code.
- [`fill_missing_depths()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/fill_missing_depths.md)
  — fix swapped upper/lower depth values and fill missing values from
  genus-level means.

#### GEBCO Bathymetry

- [`load_gebco_bathymetry()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/load_gebco_bathymetry.md)
  — load a GEBCO bathymetry NetCDF as a `SpatRaster`.

#### World Ocean Atlas 2023 utilities

- [`woa_download()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_download.md)
  — download WOA 2023 NetCDF files (temperature, salinity, dissolved
  oxygen, oxygen saturation, AOU, nitrate, phosphate, silicate, density)
  at 0.25°, 1°, or 5° resolution, with caching. Read a field with
  `as_proxy(file, var = "t_an")`, crop it, and read it with
  [`as_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_voxel.md);
  its help page lists the variable and field codes.
- [`woa_cache_dir()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_cache_dir.md)
  /
  [`woa_cache_clear()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_cache_clear.md)
  — manage the persistent WOA download cache.

#### Global Fishing Watch (fisheries effort)

- [`gfw_effort_to_raster()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/gfw_effort_to_raster.md)
  — turn the long-format apparent-fishing-hours tibble from
  [`gfwr::gfw_ais_fishing_hours()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/gfwr/man/gfw_ais_fishing_hours.html)
  into a multi-layer `SpatRaster`, one layer per gear (or other
  grouping). Extending that into 3D uses the general converters —
  [`as_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_envelope.md)
  and
  [`envelope_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/envelope_to_voxel.md)
  — driven by a gear-to-depth-band lookup. Those operating-depth priors
  are analysis assumptions rather than package data, so they live in the
  `gfw-fishing-effort-3d` article.

## Use of generative AI

Generative AI tools were used to write much of this package. This
section says how, following [rOpenSci’s AI
policy](https://ropensci.org/blog/2026/02/26/ropensci-ai-policy/).

- **Without AI:** the package grew out of analysis scripts written over
  about three years without AI, for a study of 3D overlap between
  species and fisheries in Bangladesh
  ([thesis](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:b425c41e-deb4-4bed-917e-dfdaf7b59f78))
  and for extracting environmental variables per species
  ([preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.07.16.739000v1)).
  The first version of the package, including the first `SPEC.md`, tests
  and documentation, was written by hand from those scripts.
- **With AI:** since then, most of the code, tests and documentation
  have been written with generative AI tools, mainly Claude Opus 5.5 and
  OpenAI GPT 6.1 Sol. AI is also used to review code and to draw some of
  the figures in the documentation.
- **What the authors do:** decide the package design (for example the
  `SpatVoxel` and `SpatEnvelope` classes, the build, intersect and
  summarise steps, and the data model decisions in
  [SPEC.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/SPEC.md)),
  decide what each issue should do, and review every pull request before
  it is merged.
- **How contributions are made:**
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/CONTRIBUTING.md)
  and
  [AGENTS.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/AGENTS.md)
  set the rules AI agents follow. Commits and pull requests written with
  an agent name the model in a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome. `ocean3d` is being actively built out from a
set of lab analyses into a general, tested package, and there is plenty
of well-scoped work available. Start with:

- **[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/CONTRIBUTING.md)**
  — development setup, data requirements, the branching/coordination
  workflow, and coding conventions.
- **[SPEC.md](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/SPEC.md)**
  — the roadmap; every planned function with its priority and source.
  Unchecked items are up for grabs.
- **[Code of
  Conduct](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)**.

New contributors: the “Known rough edges / good first issues” section of
`CONTRIBUTING.md` lists concrete starting points.

# Package index

## 3D classes

3D objects. A `SpatVoxel` holds values by depth level; a `SpatEnvelope`
holds a depth range per cell; a `SpatVector3D` holds points or lines
with a depth and time at each vertex, or polygons with a depth range.

- [`c(`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVoxel-class.md)
  [`subset(`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVoxel-class.md)
  [`` `[[<-`( ``*`<SpatVoxel>`*`,`*`<numeric>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVoxel-class.md)
  [`` `[[<-`( ``*`<SpatVoxel>`*`,`*`<character>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVoxel-class.md)
  [`show(`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVoxel-class.md)
  : 3D voxel model: one layer per standard depth level
- [`show(`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatEnvelope-class.md)
  : 2.5D min-max envelope: exactly depth_min, depth_max
- [`geomtype(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`length(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`show(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`` `[`( ``*`<SpatVector3D>`*`,`*`<ANY>`*`,`*`<ANY>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`ext(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`crs(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVector3D-class.md)
  : 3D points, lines and polygons with depth and time
- [`SpatVolume-class`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatVolume-class.md)
  : Union of the package's 3D domain representations
- [`depths()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/depths.md)
  : Depths of a voxel's layers
- [`depth_bounds()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/depth_bounds.md)
  : Depth edges of a voxel's layers

## Build

Turn inputs into 3D objects, and convert between them.

- [`as_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_voxel.md)
  : Create a voxel object
- [`as_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_envelope.md)
  : Coerce a 2D footprint to a 2.5D min-max envelope
- [`as_vector3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_vector3d.md)
  : Build 3D points, lines or polygons
- [`buffer_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/buffer_3d.md)
  : Buffer 3D points or lines into polygons
- [`sample_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/sample_3d.md)
  : Sample 3D lines into points
- [`vector3d_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vector3d_to_envelope.md)
  : Convert 3D polygons to an envelope on a grid
- [`vector3d_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vector3d_to_voxel.md)
  : Convert 3D polygons to a voxel on a template's grid and depth levels
- [`vect_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/vect_to_envelope.md)
  : Convert SpatVector or sf to SpatEnvelope
- [`envelope_to_voxel()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/envelope_to_voxel.md)
  : Convert Envelope 2.5D -\> Voxel 3D
- [`voxel_to_envelope()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_to_envelope.md)
  : Collapse Voxel 3D -\> Envelope 2.5D
- [`profile_flat()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_profiles.md)
  [`profile_equal()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/voxel_profiles.md)
  : Vertical profiles for voxel building
- [`occupied()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/occupied.md)
  : Reduce a variable voxel to a presence voxel
- [`create_study_raster()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/create_study_raster.md)
  : Create a study area raster grid

## Intersect

Find where 3D objects meet.

- [`intersect_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/intersect_3d.md)
  : The 3D space two objects share
- [`intersects_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/intersects_3d.md)
  : Do two objects share any 3D space?
- [`mask(`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`,`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`,`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`,`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`,`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatRaster>`*`,`*`<SpatEnvelope>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatRaster>`*`,`*`<SpatVoxel>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  [`mask(`*`<SpatRaster>`*`,`*`<SpatVector3D>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/mask-3d.md)
  : Keep a raster's values inside a 3D domain

## Summarise

Measure 3D objects and their overlap, and summarise their values.

- [`volume()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/volume.md)
  : 3D volume of a domain
- [`summarise_3d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/summarise_3d.md)
  : Summarise a voxel's values across cells and depth levels

## Extraction

Extract environmental values from netCDF files at points, in buffers,
along tracks, or from a `SpatVoxel` within an area. These run build,
intersect and summarise in one call.

- [`extract_to_point()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_point.md)
  : Extract values from netCDFs to one or more point observations
- [`extract2d()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract2d.md)
  : Extract values from a 2D netCDF variable
- [`extract3d_all()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_all.md)
  : Extract nearest, surface and bottom values from a 3D netCDF variable
- [`extract3d_bottom()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_bottom.md)
  : Extract the bottom available layer from a 3D netCDF variable
- [`extract3d_nearest()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_nearest.md)
  : Extract the nearest valid depth layer from a 3D netCDF variable
- [`extract3d_surface()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract3d_surface.md)
  : Extract the surface layer from a 3D netCDF variable
- [`extract_to_buffer()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_buffer.md)
  : Summarise environmental values around observations
- [`extract_to_track()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_track.md)
  : Extract environmental values along tracks and lines
- [`extract_to_area()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/extract_to_area.md)
  : Extract a 3D raster to an area and a depth band

## Data sources

Download, cache and load public datasets.

- [`load_gebco_bathymetry()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/load_gebco_bathymetry.md)
  : Load GEBCO bathymetry raster
- [`woa_download()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_download.md)
  : Download a WOA NetCDF file (with caching)
- [`woa_cache_dir()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_cache_dir.md)
  : WOA cache directory
- [`woa_cache_clear()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/woa_cache_clear.md)
  : Clear the WOA cache
- [`gfw_effort_to_raster()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/gfw_effort_to_raster.md)
  : Rasterise a GFW effort tibble onto a target grid
- [`fetch_species_assessments()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/fetch_species_assessments.md)
  : Fetch species assessment data from IUCN Red List API
- [`fill_missing_depths()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/fill_missing_depths.md)
  : Fill missing depth values

## Core data object (experimental)

Describe a gridded netCDF variable without reading its values. Not yet
accepted by other functions.

- [`crop(`*`<SpatProxy>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatProxy-class.md)
  [`show(`*`<SpatProxy>`*`)`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/SpatProxy-class.md)
  : A gridded dataset described but not loaded (experimental)
- [`as_proxy()`](https://marine-biodiversity-conservation-lab.github.io/ocean3d/reference/as_proxy.md)
  : Describe gridded data without reading its values (experimental)
